name: Whist Israeli
description: Four-player exact-bid trick-taking game popular in Israel. No partnerships; each player bids how many tricks they will take. Two-phase bidding sets contract and trick bids; scoring by exact bid (10 plus square of tricks) or penalty for off.

overview.description: Four-player exact-bid trick-taking game popular in Israel. No partnerships; each player bids how many tricks they will take. Two-phase bidding sets contract and trick bids; scoring by exact bid (10 plus square of tricks) or penalty for off.

history.origins: Popular in Israel where it is just called Whist. Classified as an exact-bidding game; no partnerships, unlike classic Whist.
timeline: 20th century: Popular in Israel as exact-bid Whist; no partnerships; distinct from classic Whist.

setup.players: Four players, no partnerships; play is clockwise. A standard 52-card pack is used; each player receives 13 cards. First dealer is chosen at random; the turn to deal passes to the left after each hand.
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles and cuts; all 52 cards dealt one at a time so each player has 13. First dealer chosen at random; turn to deal passes left after each hand.

rules.objective: Each player aims to take exactly the number of tricks they bid in the second phase. Score 10 plus the square of tricks for exact bid; lose 10 per trick over or under. Zero bid has special scoring. First to reach agreed target score wins.
rules.gameplay: Two-phase bidding: first phase (dealer starts, clockwise) bids 5-13 tricks plus suit or no trumps (Bridge order: no trumps highest, then spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). After four consecutive passes, last bidder is declarer and trump is set. Second phase: other three players (declarer's left clockwise) each bid number of tricks (0+); fourth player cannot bid so total equals 13. Game is over if total>13, under if <13. Declarer leads; must follow suit; highest trump wins trick else highest of led suit. Winner of trick leads next. After 13 tricks, score each player.

strategy.basic: Bid conservatively; track which cards are out; try to take exactly your bid and hinder others from making theirs.

variations.name: Gulash
variations.description: If all four pass in first bidding, do not redeal. Each player passes three cards face down to the left (select before seeing received cards). Then bidding starts again. If all pass again, pass three more left and rebid. If all pass a third time, throw in and redeal by same dealer.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Gulash only changes pass-and-rebid procedure; no engine constant overrides documented.

scoring.description: Exact bid: 10 plus square of tricks; off by N tricks: minus 10N. Zero bid: fail -50 for first trick then +10 each; zero made under 50, over 30. Cumulative total; game ends when one reaches agreed target; highest wins; tie broken by further hands.
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach or exceed the agreed target score wins. Tie: play further hands until one player has highest total.

synthesis.shortDescription: Four-player exact-bid trick-taking popular in Israel; two-phase bidding, score by exact tricks.
